levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis Linux backdoor. The backdoor is known to be a modular trojan with C2 capabilities. Your mission is to identify, analyze, and contain this threat within our test environment.

**Scenario Objectives:**
1. Identify suspicious services and processes
2. Investigate persistence mechanisms
3. Analyze C2 communication patterns
4. Contain and eradicate the threat

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the credentials provided. Enter 'start' to begin. Username: investigator, Password: SecurePass123
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the credentials provided. Enter 'start' to begin. Username: investigator, Password: SecurePass123

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring system logs on target, you noticed unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on this host to identify any suspicious or unauthorized services.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `ps aux`. Look for any services or processes that are unusual or unexpected. The suspicious service in this scenario is the `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for anything unusual or unexpected.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `ps aux` to list running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you've identified a suspicious service, determine how it maintains persistence on the system. Investigate how this service is automatically started after system reboots.
levels.solution: To investigate persistence mechanisms, check systemd services and timers. Use commands like `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` and `systemctl list-timers`. The suspicious service `bkd.service` is set to start automatically.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check systemd services and timers for anything related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` and `systemctl list-timers` to investigate persistence mechanisms.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication.
levels.solution: To identify the C2 communication port, monitor network connections associated with the suspicious service. Use commands like `ss -tulnp` or `netstat -tulnp`. The suspicious service is communicating on port 80.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Monitor network connections associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `ss -tulnp` or `netstat -tulnp` to monitor network connections.
